questions.text: The only commandment which has a promise attached to it concerns
options: not taking the name of the Lord in vain
questions.explanation: The fifth commandment, honoring parents, has a promise of long life.

questions.text: 'What is sweeter than honey?' 'What is stronger than lion?' Who gave this riddle?
questions.explanation: Samson gave this riddle at his wedding feast.

questions.text: 'Draw your sword and kill me, lest men say of me, 'A woman killed him.'' The speaker was
questions.explanation: Abimelech asked his armor-bearer to kill him so it wouldn't be said a woman killed him.

questions.text: A famous prophetess who was also a judge in Israel was
questions.explanation: Deborah was both a prophetess and a judge in Israel.

questions.text: Gideon was also called Jerubbaal because he
options: pulled down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it
led the Israelites against the Midianites who were Baal Worshipers
turned Israel away from Baal worship
questions.explanation: Gideon was called Jerubbaal because he pulled down the altar of Baal.

questions.text: Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom because
options: he did everything as the Lord had commanded him
Moses had laid his hand upon him
the Lord had promised to be with him as He was with Moses
he meditated on the book of the law day and night
questions.explanation: Joshua had the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him.

questions.text: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins' means that in comparison with his father
questions.explanation: Rehoboam said this, indicating he would be harsher than his father.

questions.text: 'What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, O Israel!....' This declaration marked the end of
questions.explanation: This declaration marked the end of the united kingdom of Israel.

questions.text: The incident which inspired King Josiah to undertake a reform was the
options: discovery of the book of the law
questions.explanation: Josiah's reform was inspired by the discovery of the book of the law.

questions.text: 'Seek good, and not evil that you may live; and so the Lord, the God of hosts, will be with you have said...' Which prophet gave this advice?
questions.explanation: Amos gave this advice to the people of Israel.

questions.text: '... O Lord, answer me, that this people may know that thou, O Lord, art God, and that thou had turned their hearts back.' What happened after this prayer?
options: The fire of the Lord fell.
questions.explanation: Fire fell from heaven and consumed the sacrifice.

questions.text: One of the reasons why Sennacherib could not enter Jerusalem and conquer it as he did to Samaria was that
options: his god told him to return home from his camp
thousands of his soldiers miraculously died overnight
he willingly changed his mind and returned to his country
fight broke out among his soldiers
questions.explanation: The angel of the Lord killed 185,000 Assyrian soldiers overnight.

questions.text: When the Chaldean army captured King Zedekiah, they
options: slew his wives before his eyes
cut off his fingers and toes
questions.explanation: The Chaldeans cut off Zedekiah's sons and put out his eyes.

questions.text: 'All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all.' This messianic prophecy was made by
questions.explanation: Isaiah made this prophecy about the suffering servant.

questions.text: The vision of 'dry bones' teaches that
options: there will be a resurrection of the body
there will be a new creation
questions.explanation: The vision teaches that exiled Israel will be restored.

questions.text: Gilgamesh Epic is the Babylonian equivalent of the biblical story of the
questions.explanation: The Gilgamesh Epic contains a flood story similar to Noah's.

questions.text: To whom was the birth of Jesus announced with a sign?
questions.explanation: The angel announced Jesus' birth to the shepherds with the sign of a baby in a manger.

questions.text: The central message of John the Baptist in the Jordan region was about a baptism
questions.explanation: John preached a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

questions.text: Jesus heard a voice saying: 'Thou art my beloved son; with thee I am well pleased.' Jesus heard this voice during His
questions.explanation: The voice spoke at Jesus' baptism.

questions.text: According to Herod, Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead because He
options: was a prophet like one of the prophets
had the powers of John at work in him
questions.explanation: Herod thought Jesus had the powers of John at work in Him.

questions.text: When John sent his disciples to ask Jesus 'Are you the one who is to come...?' Jesus' immediate reaction was to
options: ask them to tell John about his miracles
speak to the crowds concerning John
ask the crowds what they went into the wilderness to see
questions.explanation: Jesus told them to tell John what they saw and heard.

questions.text: 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among men with whom he is pleased!' is usually referred to as
questions.explanation: This is the angels' song at Jesus' birth.

questions.text: 'I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.' This statement was made during the healing of the
questions.explanation: Jesus commended the centurion's faith in healing his servant.

questions.text: When they saw the man who had been possessed by demons in his right mind, the Gerasenes
options: asked Jesus to depart from them
asked Jesus to stay on with them
questions.explanation: The Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them.

questions.text: One of the objectives, according to Mark, for which Jesus appointed the twelve, was for them to
options: make disciples of all the nations of the earth
denounce the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and the Sadducees
questions.explanation: Jesus appointed the twelve to cast out demons.

questions.text: 'Get behind me, Satan! For you are not on the side of God, but of men.' The reason for this sharp rebuke was that the addressee
options: confessed that Jesus is the Christ.
wanted to dissuade Jesus from dying on the cross
desired to be at the right hand of Christ
questions.explanation: Peter tried to dissuade Jesus from going to the cross.

questions.text: From the Parable of the friend at midnight we learn that
options: we should always make our requests even at midnight
we cannot receive anything from God if we don't ask
an evil father will always give good gifts to his children
the heavenly Father will always give the Holy Spirit to anybody
questions.explanation: The parable teaches persistence in prayer.

questions.text: 'And he was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered to him.' Jesus was led into the wilderness by
questions.explanation: Jesus was led into the wilderness by the Holy Spirit.

questions.text: Which of the following instructions was given only to the seventy and not to the twelve when Jesus sent His disciples on missions?
options: Wipe off the dust from their feet
Salute no one on the road
questions.explanation: The instruction to salute no one on the road was given only to the seventy.

questions.text: 'But new wine must be put into fresh wine-skins.' What issue was raised to which this statement was a response?
questions.explanation: Jesus responded this way when asked about fasting.

questions.text: 'Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the things that are God's.' The above quotation teaches
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that we should obey civil authority where it is due.

questions.text: Who requested for the body of Jesus after His death?
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea requested Jesus' body from Pilate.

questions.text: 'Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us ...?' This expresses the regret of
questions.explanation: Cleopas and the other disciple said this on the road to Emmaus.

questions.text: Paul was accused of apparently being a preacher of foreign divinities in Athens because he preached Jesus and the
questions.explanation: Paul preached Jesus and the resurrection, leading to accusations of preaching foreign gods.

questions.text: When Paul and Barnabas healed a cripple at Lystra, the people named them
questions.explanation: The people called Barnabas Zeus (Jupiter) and Paul Hermes (Mercury).

questions.text: Paul told the Athenians that they were very religious because
options: some of their poets said that men are the offsprings of God.
they dedicated an altar to the Unknown God.
their Epicurean and Stoic philosophers always discussed religious issues.
the city was full of idols and symbols of religious devotion.
questions.explanation: Paul noted the city was full of idols, showing their religiosity.

questions.text: The elders at Jerusalem advised Paul on his arrival in the city to
options: purify himself along with men under vows
join those in the temple for prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: The elders advised Paul to purify himself with four men under vows.

questions.text: 'Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you, and no man shall attack you to harm you; for I have many people in this city.' The city referred to was
questions.explanation: The Lord spoke this to Paul in Corinth.

questions.text: To the question of the Philippian Jailer, 'Men, what must I do to be saved?' Paul replied,
options: confess your sins and give alms
release us and wash our wounds
trust in God and pray always
questions.explanation: Paul told the jailer to believe in the Lord Jesus.

questions.text: 'Let it be known to you then that if this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, they will listen.' This implies that
options: the Gentiles will be more receptive to Christianity than the Jews
the Jews have lost the opportunity of salvation forever.
Paul has completely lost hope in the Jews.
questions.explanation: Paul indicated that the Gentiles would be more receptive to the gospel.

questions.text: During the voyage to Rome, some people thought that Paul was a god because
options: he was not harmed by a viper
questions.explanation: The people of Malta thought Paul was a god when he survived a viper's bite.

questions.text: 'Be fruitful and multiply...' This statement occurs first in Genesis following the creation of
questions.explanation: God blessed Adam and Eve with this command.

questions.text: '... Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for God made man in his own image...' The above passage explains the
questions.explanation: This passage explains the origin of blood revenge.

questions.text: The four promises of God to Abram were land,
options: Many descendants, greatness and medium of blessings
questions.explanation: God promised Abram many descendants, greatness, and that he would be a blessing.

questions.text: 'God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh over me.' This statement was made at the birth of
questions.explanation: Sarah said this at the birth of Isaac.

questions.text: The main point emphasized in the story of Joseph's treatment of his brothers in Egypt was that
options: God's design for anybody cannot be stopped
it is good to forgive one's enemies
one should test any old enemy before trusting him
questions.explanation: Joseph recognized that God's purpose was at work.

questions.text: 'Put off your shoes from your feet; for the place where you stand is holy.' Where was this statement made?
questions.explanation: God spoke this to Moses at Mount Horeb (Sinai).

questions.text: When the Israelites were caught between Pharaoh's army and the Red Sea, God instructed Moses to
options: command the sea to be divided
throw his rod into the sea
stretch out his hand over the sea
questions.explanation: Moses was to stretch out his hand over the sea.

questions.text: 'Who is the Lord that I should heed his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and moreover I will not let Israel go.' What was Pharaoh's response to this?
options: He appealed to them to stay in Egypt
questions.explanation: Pharaoh increased the Israelites' burden by making them work harder.

questions.text: Which of the following is a condition for the eating of the Passover?
options: A fatted lamb should be taken from among the sheep or goat
Anything that remained until morning should be burnt
The lamb should be eaten boiled with its head, legs and inner parts.
It should not be eaten in haste.
questions.explanation: Anything left until morning was to be burned.

questions.text: Before God met with Israel at Mount Sinai, Moses charged his people not to
options: tremble at the sight of smoke
tremble at the sound of thunder
questions.explanation: Moses told the people not to go near a woman before meeting God.

questions.text: 'It is not the sound of shouting for victory, or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear.' This was said after the
options: consecration of the Israelites at Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Joshua heard singing when the people were worshipping the golden calf.

questions.text: In order to stay alive, anyone who was bitten by the fiery serpent had to
questions.explanation: Anyone who looked at the bronze serpent would live.

questions.text: '... As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you...' In the above passage, God addresses
questions.explanation: God spoke these words to Joshua.

questions.text: The cities of the Amorites were completely devastated by Israel through the combined forces of
questions.explanation: Israel defeated the Amorites through panic, hailstone, and sword.

questions.text: In which Philistine city did Samson carry away on his shoulder, the doors, posts and bar of the city gate?
questions.explanation: Samson carried the gate of Gaza away.

questions.text: The king that reigned in Samaria during the prophecies of Amos and Hosea was
questions.explanation: Jeroboam II, son of Joash, reigned during Amos and Hosea's prophecies.

questions.text: The king who disguised himself when he traveled to Ramoth-gilead was
questions.explanation: Ahab disguised himself before going to Ramoth-gilead.

questions.text: Which of the following kings built the city of Samaria?
questions.explanation: Omri built the city of Samaria.

questions.text: The theme of Amos's prophecies centres on the
questions.explanation: Amos emphasized God's righteousness.

questions.text: The event which ultimately led to the destruction of the Northern Kingdom was the invasion of
questions.explanation: Syria was invaded by Assyria and Judah, leading to the fall of the Northern Kingdom.

questions.text: What was king Hezekiah's reaction to the letter of threat from the Assyrian king?
options: He spread it before God in the temple and prayed
He sent for his fellow kings to come and assist him
He summoned his soldiers to fight the Assyrians
He sent to the prophets for advice
questions.explanation: Hezekiah spread the letter before the Lord and prayed.

questions.text: Manasseh did what was evil in the sight of the Lord because he
options: waged wars against the people of God
questions.explanation: Manasseh encouraged idol worship in Judah.

questions.text: Who was the last king of Judah that suffered at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah; Babylon conquered Jerusalem during his reign.

questions.text: The image of jealousy which Ezekiel saw was the
options: worship of Baal in the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw an image of jealousy in the temple.

questions.text: What reason did the people around Jerusalem give for wanting to assist the returned exiles in rebuilding the temple?
options: They shared the same geographical location with the Jews
They themselves were Jews by descent
They were commanded to do so by king Cyrus of Persia
They also worshipped the same God as the Jews
questions.explanation: They claimed to be Jews by descent and worshipped the same God.

questions.text: Jeremiah's vision of the rod of almond was meant to symbolize that God
options: would protect Jeremiah at all times
would confirm His word through Jeremiah
would send evil from the North upon the people
had appointed Jeremiah as a prophet before his birth
questions.explanation: The rod of almond symbolized that God would send evil from the North.

questions.text: 'Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel...' This meant that
questions.explanation: Simeon prophesied that many would fall and rise because of Jesus.

questions.text: '... Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?' This was said to
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to Joseph and Mary when they found Him in the temple.

questions.text: '... Rob no one by violence or by false accusation, and be content with your wages.' This was said to
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this to tax collectors.

questions.text: '... The heaven was opened, and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form, as a dove, and a voice came...' This occurred when Jesus was
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit descended on Jesus at His baptism.

questions.text: James and John caused the other disciples of Jesus to be angry because they
options: did not go with the others on the missionary journey
asked for a special favour to sit with Jesus in glory
deflected to join the disciples of John the Baptist
questions.explanation: James and John asked for special seats in Jesus' glory, making the other disciples angry.

questions.text: What is the significance of Jesus allowing His disciples to take certain things and not others on their missionary journey to the evangelist?
options: Adequate material and spiritual preparation should be made for the work
He should depend on his audience for every need
He should have absolute confidence in the sufficiency of God
He should not leave a place where he is not received without placing a curse on the people
questions.explanation: Jesus taught absolute confidence in God's sufficiency.

questions.text: '... Moses and Elijah, who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure...' This event was the
questions.explanation: Moses and Elijah spoke of Jesus' departure (ascension) at the transfiguration.

questions.text: Jesus pronounced 'woe' on the rich during the sermon on the plain because they
options: had received their reward on earth
questions.explanation: Jesus said the rich had already received their reward on earth.

questions.text: In the parable of the sower, the seeds that fell on the rock represent people who
options: believed for a short while and later fell away
believed and were later enticed by riches
questions.explanation: The rocky ground represents those who believe for a while but fall away.

questions.text: 'Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?' Jesus told the rich young ruler to
options: keep the commandments and surrender his wealth
keep the commandments and pay tithe
do to others as he wished others to do him
questions.explanation: Jesus told him to keep the commandments and sell his possessions.

questions.text: 'Go your way; your faith has made you well.' This statement was addressed to
options: the woman with the issue of blood
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to Bartimaeus the blind beggar.

questions.text: The disciples could not cast out the dumb spirit because
options: they were not familiar with that particular spirit
it could only be driven out by prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: Jesus said this kind could only be driven out by prayer and fasting.

questions.text: Which of the following did NOT believe in the resurrection of the dead?
questions.explanation: The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection.

questions.text: The Holy week starts with the
questions.explanation: Holy Week begins with Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

questions.text: Where did Jesus go after His triumphal entry into Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jesus went to Bethany after His triumphal entry.

questions.text: Pilate delivered Jesus to be crucified because he
options: was afraid of the chief priests
questions.explanation: Pilate delivered Jesus to satisfy the crowd's demand.

questions.text: The two disciples on the way to Emmaus recognized Jesus
options: before they got to the village
at the breaking of bread while at table
questions.explanation: They recognized Jesus when He broke bread with them.

questions.text: 'Then after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.' The significance of the laying on the hands in this passage is that
options: the Church under the guidance of the Holy Spirit initiated the missionary work of Paul and Barnabas
the teachers' and prophets' hands conferred authority on Paul and Barnabas
the Apostles, Paul and Barnabas were here ordained priests
Paul and Barnabas were here confirmed Christians and the first Apostles
questions.explanation: The laying on of hands signified the church commissioning Paul and Barnabas under the Holy Spirit.

questions.text: The reason for the first Apostolic Council in Jerusalem was that
options: circumcision was enjoined on the Gentile converts as necessary for salvation
the Gentiles were discriminated against at the fellowship meals
the widows of Hellenistic Jews were discriminated against in the daily ministration
questions.explanation: The council was called because some taught that circumcision was necessary for salvation.

questions.text: Before the Areopagus, Paul declared that the Unknown God was
options: a manifestation of the human mind
questions.explanation: Paul declared that the Unknown God was the creator of all things.

questions.text: Owing to the uproar in Jerusalem, the tribune ordered Paul to be examined by scourging, but changed his mind when he discovered that Paul was
questions.explanation: The tribune stopped the examination when he learned Paul was a Roman citizen.

questions.text: When Paul and his companions were shipwrecked, the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners but the centurion prevented them because
options: they would have to account for them
he wanted to save Paul's life
it was not lawful to kill
questions.explanation: The centurion prevented the killing to save Paul's life.

questions.text: '... You shall indeed hear but never understand and you shall indeed see but never perceive.' To which prophet did Paul attribute this saying?
questions.explanation: Paul quoted Isaiah's prophecy.

questions.text: On arrival in Rome, Paul first addressed
questions.explanation: Paul first addressed the Jewish leaders in Rome.

questions.text: 'I heard the sound of thee in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.' The question that immediately followed this statement was
options: 'What is this that you have done?'
'Who told you that you are naked?'
'Have you eaten of the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?'
questions.explanation: God asked Adam, 'Where are you?'

questions.text: One of the rules given to Noah after the flood was that he should
options: not eat the flesh with its blood
questions.explanation: Noah was forbidden from eating flesh with its blood.

questions.text: '... Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you ...' This statement was made by
questions.explanation: Isaac blessed Jacob with these words.

questions.text: 'This lad is gone; and where shall I go?' Which of Joseph's brothers uttered these words?
questions.explanation: Reuben said this after Joseph was sold.

questions.text: Pharaoh oppressed the Israelites because
options: he feared that they might join his enemies to fight him
they continued to give birth to male children
they refused to worship the Egyptian gods
questions.explanation: Pharaoh feared the Israelites might join his enemies.

questions.text: '... The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to be still...' The Lord fought for the people of Israel on the occasion referred to in the statement by
options: drowning the Egyptian army in the Red Sea
opening a chasm in the earth and swallowing their enemies
raining fire and brimstone on their enemies
raining hail and stones on their enemies
questions.explanation: The Lord fought by drowning the Egyptian army in the Red Sea.

questions.text: When Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, the Israelites
options: decided to go back to Egypt
went up to look for him
asked Aaron to make gods for them
questions.explanation: The people asked Aaron to make them gods when Moses delayed.

questions.text: Moses could not enter the Promised Land because he
options: was too old to cross the border
was too busy preparing his successor
did not give due regard to God
questions.explanation: Moses did not give due regard to God at Meribah.

questions.text: Moses consecrated Joshua as the new leader of Israel in the presence of
questions.explanation: Moses consecrated Joshua before Eleazar the priest.

questions.text: 'All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go. Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you...' This pledge was made to Joshua by the
options: Reubenites, the Gadites and part of the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh pledged this to Joshua.

questions.text: Rahab the harlot assisted the Israelite spies as they prepared to attack
options: the five kings of the Amorites
questions.explanation: Rahab helped the spies attack Jericho.

questions.text: 'Out of the eater came something to eat. Out of the strong came something sweet.' This riddle was explained first to Samson's
questions.explanation: Samson's friends demanded the answer to his riddle.

questions.text: For offending God, the Israelites were delivered into the power of Midian for
questions.explanation: The Israelites were oppressed by Midian for seven years.

questions.text: Gideon was able to defeat the Midianites with a reduced number of soldiers because he
questions.explanation: Gideon trusted in God's power, not his own strength.

questions.text: Elkanah would give Hannah only one portion of the sacrifice because
questions.explanation: Elkanah gave Hannah one portion because he loved her despite her barrenness.

questions.text: Who was unfaithful to her husband as Israel was to God?
questions.explanation: Gomer was unfaithful to Hosea, symbolizing Israel's unfaithfulness to God.

questions.text: '... To your tents O Israel!' This was a signal for
questions.explanation: This was a signal of rebellion against the house of David.

questions.text: 'As the Lord God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain those years except by my words.' Who was the Israelite king during the period of the drought?
questions.explanation: Ahab was king during the drought declared by Elijah.

questions.text: When Elisha received the message about Benhadad's ill-health, the prophet wept because
options: Benhadad would not recover from the sickness
Hazael would be cruel to Israel
questions.explanation: Elisha wept because Hazael would bring great harm to Israel.

questions.text: '... Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear, open thy eyes, O Lord, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to mock the living God...' This was the prayer of
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed this prayer against Sennacherib.

questions.text: '... Behold, I am bringing upon Jerusalem and Judah such evil that the ears of every one who hears of it will tingle...' The above was said because of the sins of
questions.explanation: This judgment was pronounced because of Manasseh's sins.

questions.text: Saul initially desired to kill David because
options: David became very popular after killing Goliath
David married Michal and befriended Jonathan
Saul was tormented by an evil spirit
questions.explanation: Saul became jealous of David's popularity after he killed Goliath.

questions.text: God revealed to Solomon that the kingdom would be divided after him because he
questions.explanation: Solomon's heart turned from God as he worshipped other gods.

questions.text: 'In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and His train filled the temple.' Which prophet is associated with this vision?
questions.explanation: Isaiah saw this vision in the year King Uzziah died.

questions.text: King Herod granted the request of the daughter of Herodias by beheading John the Baptist because
options: the King was impressed by the way she danced
John the Baptist opposed the king's love affairs with Herodias
Herod was bound by oath and personal integrity
Herod was anxious to see John the Baptist dead
questions.explanation: Herod was bound by his oath before many witnesses.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a condition for being a disciple of Jesus?
options: Having a good knowledge of the scriptures
Taking up of the cross daily
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that discipleship requires self-denial, taking up the cross, and confessing Him.

questions.text: According to Mark's Gospel, the first miracle of Jesus was
options: opening the eyes of a blind man
healing a man with an unclean spirit
raising a dead boy to life
questions.explanation: Mark records Jesus' first miracle as healing a man with an unclean spirit.

questions.text: When the disciples thought that the kingdom of God was to appear immediately, Jesus told them the parable of the
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable of the pounds to correct their expectation of immediate arrival.

questions.text: The miracle which Jesus performed on the Sabbath was the healing of the
questions.explanation: Jesus healed the man with a withered hand on the Sabbath.

questions.text: Peace makers are blessed because they shall
options: be called the sons of God
questions.explanation: Jesus said peacemakers shall be called sons of God.

questions.text: 'He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me, ...' The above statement was addressed to
options: the 12 whom he sent out to preach
all the disciples, just before the Ascension
the 70 whom he sent out to preach
all the disciples during the Sermon on the Mount
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to the twelve disciples when sending them out.

questions.text: 'A great Prophet has arisen among us! and God has visited his people.' These statements were made during the
options: raising of the son of the widow of Nain
questions.explanation: The crowd said this after Jesus raised the widow's son at Nain.

questions.text: Jesus gave the sign of Jonah to the Pharisees to indicate His
options: three-fold office as Prophet, Priest and King
questions.explanation: The sign of Jonah pointed to Jesus' death and resurrection.

questions.text: The Jews asked Jesus whether they should pay their tax or not because they wanted to
options: help him and his disciples to pay taxes
questions.explanation: The Jews asked this question to trap Jesus.

questions.text: Jesus began to teach His disciples about His suffering, rejection, crucifixion and resurrection after
options: the healing of the blind Bartimaeus
questions.explanation: After Peter's confession, Jesus began teaching about His death and resurrection.

questions.text: '... For the Son of man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.' This statement was made by Jesus
options: after healing two blind men near Jericho
immediately before he told the parable of the householder
during the discussion that followed the request of the sons of Zebedee
as he was foretelling his crucifixion and resurrection
questions.explanation: Jesus said this after James and John requested special positions.

questions.text: Herod was very glad to see Jesus at the trial because
options: John the Baptist spoke to him about Jesus
he believed that Jesus was the Messiah
he hoped to see Jesus perform some miracles
the quarrel between Herod and Pilate was settled on account of Jesus
questions.explanation: Herod hoped to see Jesus perform a miracle.

questions.text: 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!' This verse is connected with
options: the song of the disciples after the Last Supper
questions.explanation: This was shouted during Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

questions.text: According to Mark, the people who saw where Jesus was laid were Mary Magdalene and
questions.explanation: Mark records Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James seeing where Jesus was laid.

questions.text: The message of the risen Christ to the woman who came early to the tomb was to be relayed to the disciples and to
questions.explanation: Jesus specifically asked to tell Peter about His resurrection.

questions.text: 'I have no silver and gold, but I give you what I have; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.' This was said by Peter to a lame man
questions.explanation: Peter healed the lame man at the gate called Beautiful.

questions.text: The immediate cause of the stoning of Stephen was his
options: declaration of Jesus as the Righteous One
condemnation of the Jewish rite of circumcision
claiming to see Jesus at the right hand of God
questions.explanation: Stephen was stoned after claiming to see Jesus at God's right hand.

questions.text: 'But when they recognized that he was a Jew, for about two hours they all with one voice cried out, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!'' Who was the Jew alluded to here?
questions.explanation: The Ephesians cried out against Paul, though Alexander was also involved.

questions.text: Saul and Barnabas were sent on their mission by the
questions.explanation: Saul and Barnabas were sent out by the church at Antioch.

questions.text: The Jerusalem Council sent a group of four with a letter to Antioch. At the end of their mission, which of the following remained behind in Antioch?
questions.explanation: Judas and Silas remained in Antioch.

questions.text: 'They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men who are Roman citizens, and have thrown us into prison; and do they now cast us out secretly?...' This experience of Paul was in
questions.explanation: Paul and Silas were beaten and imprisoned in Philippi.

questions.text: Paul purified himself in the Temple after the third missionary journey because he was
options: advised to do so by the elders
questions.explanation: The elders advised Paul to purify himself.

questions.text: During Paul's trial by the Tribunal, he brought a division between the Pharisees and Sadducees by mentioning the issue of
questions.explanation: Paul said he was on trial because of the resurrection of the dead, dividing the council.

questions.text: On the Island of Malta, Paul healed a man who was
questions.explanation: Paul healed Publius' father, who was sick with dysentery.

questions.text: 'Your blood is upon your heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.' The above statement was made by
questions.explanation: Paul said this to the Jews in Rome when they rejected the gospel.

questions.text: What was upon the face of the deep on the first day of creation?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:2 says darkness was upon the face of the deep.

questions.text: 'Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to separate the day from the night...' This statement was made by God on the
questions.explanation: God created lights on the fourth day.

questions.text: The story of the Fall teaches that
options: man was made in the image of God
it is a sin to disobey God
Adam was less guilty than Eve
questions.explanation: The Fall teaches that disobedience to God is sin.

questions.text: 'On that day all the fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of the heavens were opened.' The result of this was
questions.explanation: This resulted in the great flood of heavy rain.

questions.text: 'Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would suckle children?...'
questions.explanation: Abraham said this after Isaac was born.

questions.text: The quotation, 'Let me not look upon the death of the child' comes from the story about
options: the expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael
Moses when he was placed on the bank of the Nile
questions.explanation: Hagar cried out when Ishmael was dying in the wilderness.

questions.text: Joseph's dream about his future leadership of his brothers was fulfilled when he became
options: the second in command of Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Joseph became the second in command over Egypt.

questions.text: The children of Israel cried out to God for help in Egypt because
options: Moses failed to look after them
questions.explanation: Israel cried out because they were in bondage in Egypt.

questions.text: 'What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?' The above statement was made by
questions.explanation: Pharaoh and his servants regretted letting Israel go.

questions.text: The manna which the Israelites left till the morning in disobedience to God
questions.explanation: The manna bred worms and became foul when left overnight.

questions.text: God gave the ten commandments to the people of Israel because He
options: wanted their days to be long
redeemed them from slavery in Egypt
frowned at those who took His Name in vain
questions.explanation: God gave the law after redeeming Israel from Egypt.

questions.text: '...Choose this day whom you will serve, ... as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The Israelites' response to the above statement was '...we
options: also will serve the LORD, for He is our God'
cannot serve the LORD, for He is a holy God'
will serve the LORD, for He has been good to us'
will serve the LORD, for He is a great God'
questions.explanation: The people pledged to serve the Lord as well.

questions.text: God's anger was kindled against Eli and his children because Eli did not
options: train his children in the way of the LORD
apply appropriate sanctions on his children when due
know the gravity of their actions
questions.explanation: Eli failed to restrain his sons from their sinful behavior.

questions.text: The prophets whom Saul met at Gibeah-elohim as confirmation that the LORD had anointed him to rule over God's people, were
questions.explanation: Saul met a band of ecstatic prophets as confirmation.

questions.text: While David was being anointed king, he received
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the Lord came upon David at his anointing.

questions.text: Against whom were the Israelites fighting when King David committed adultery with Uriah's wife?
questions.explanation: Israel was fighting the Ammonites when David committed adultery.

questions.text: According to Psalm 51, the sacrifice acceptable to God is
questions.explanation: David said a broken and contrite heart is the sacrifice God desires.

questions.text: Solomon could devote his attention to the building of the house of the LORD because
options: of the supplies from the Queen of Sheba
there was neither adversary nor misfortune
of David's purchase of the site for the building
questions.explanation: God gave Solomon peace with no adversaries so he could build the temple.

questions.text: The immediate cause of the division of the kingdom was
questions.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the elders' counsel, leading to division.

questions.text: 'Arise go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you.' What exactly necessitated this event?
options: The drought caused by Elijah's curse
Ahab's evil in the sight of the LORD
The ravens ceased to feed Elijah
questions.explanation: The drought had dried up the brook Cherith, so God sent Elijah to Zarephath.

questions.text: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, ...' is a hymn of praise by
options: the Virgin Mary at the Annunciation
Zechariah at the birth of John the Baptist
Simeon at the presentation of Jesus in the Temple
Elizabeth at the visit of Mary
questions.explanation: Zechariah sang this hymn after John's birth.

questions.text: According to the birth and infancy narratives in St. Matthew, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream three times. In the second appearance, he instructed Joseph to
options: accept that Mary was a virgin
questions.explanation: The angel appeared to Joseph and told him to take the child to Egypt.

questions.text: 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word; for mine eyes have seen thy salvation...' This was said at the dedication of Jesus by
questions.explanation: Simeon sang this song when he saw Jesus at the temple.

questions.text: 'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' This was addressed to
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this to the Pharisees and Sadducees.

questions.text: The second temptation of Jesus according to Luke's account of the gospel was
options: giving the kingdoms of the world to Jesus if he would worship the devil
a command for a stone to become bread
jumping down from the pinnacle of the temple
denying the name of God, the Father
questions.explanation: In Luke, the second temptation was to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

questions.text: What did Christ say should be the qualification of whoever was to be first or great among the apostles?
options: Giving one's life as a ransom
Drinking from the same cup as Jesus
questions.explanation: Jesus said whoever would be great must be a servant of all.

questions.text: A would-be disciple, who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, lacks
questions.explanation: Looking back indicates a lack of total commitment.

questions.text: In which miracle story was Jesus mistaken for a ghost by his disciples?
options: The feeding of the five thousand
Calming of the storm and sea
questions.explanation: The disciples thought Jesus was a ghost when He walked on the sea.

questions.text: According to Luke, the healing of the paralytic was intended to show that
options: Jesus has authority to forgive sins
the Holy Spirit makes intercession for sinners
questions.explanation: Jesus healed the paralytic to demonstrate His authority to forgive sins.

questions.text: '...I adjure you by God, do not torment me, ...' What is the significance of this statement?
options: The demons wanted to reach an agreement with Jesus.
It is a recognition of the fact that demons are subject to Jesus.
It shows that demons hate Jesus.
questions.explanation: The demons recognized that Jesus had authority over them.

questions.text: The story of the healing of blind Bartimaeus teaches that
options: prayer is very basic to healing
there is need to persistently shout for attention
Jesus is the Son of David
faith is a pre-requisite to healing
questions.explanation: Bartimaeus' faith was key to his healing.

questions.text: The parable of the prodigal son emphasizes that
options: it is not good for the son and the father to quarrel
the father loves the second son more than the first
questions.explanation: The parable emphasizes repentance and reconciliation.

questions.text: According to Matthew's account of the gospel, the most important divine requirement for entering the kingdom of heaven is
questions.explanation: Jesus said only those who do the Father's will enter the kingdom.

questions.text: After their mission, the seventy disciples reported to Jesus that
options: they enjoyed the hospitality of people
demons were subject to them in His name
questions.explanation: The seventy reported that even demons were subject to them in Jesus' name.

questions.text: The appearance of Moses and Elijah at the transfiguration underscores the importance in the ministry of Jesus of
questions.explanation: Moses represents the law and Elijah represents the prophets.

questions.text: 'This is my beloved Son; listen to him'. This was said on the occasion of Jesus'
questions.explanation: This was spoken at the transfiguration.

questions.text: '...My house shall be a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers.' Just before making this statement, the speaker
options: drove out those who sold in the temple
questions.explanation: Jesus drove out those who were buying and selling in the temple.

questions.text: Which of the following questions did the high priest ask Jesus during His trial?
options: 'Are you the Christ, the son of the Blessed?'
'Are you the King of the Jews?'
questions.explanation: The high priest asked Jesus if He was the Christ, the Son of God.

questions.text: '...Do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children...' These words were addressed by Jesus to the
questions.explanation: Jesus addressed these words to the daughters of Jerusalem on the way to the cross.

questions.text: What was the first statement of Jesus on the cross according to Luke's account of the gospel?
options: 'Today you shall be with me in paradise.'
'Father forgive them for they do not know what they do.'
questions.explanation: Luke records Jesus saying, 'Father forgive them' first.

questions.text: Very early in the morning, on the first day of the week, three women went to the tomb of Jesus to
options: see whether the soldiers had carried the body away
questions.explanation: The women went to anoint Jesus' body with spices.

questions.text: '...Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified...' As a reaction to this declaration, the Jews
options: decided to kill Peter and the apostles
went back to their houses in anger
were deeply troubled and asked what they should do
questions.explanation: The people were cut to the heart and asked what they should do.

questions.text: '...You have not lied to men but to God.' The immediate effect of this statement of Peter on the liar was that he
questions.explanation: Ananias fell down dead after Peter's words.

questions.text: The apostles created a new office in the ministry besides prayer and preaching, in order to address the problems of
questions.explanation: The deacons were appointed to address injustice in the distribution of food.

questions.text: Saul's encounter with the Risen Christ on the road to Damascus convinced him that
options: Jesus is the Son of God
the faith of his father was right
he should have gone to Damascus with more armed escort
questions.explanation: Saul was convinced that Jesus is the Son of God.

questions.text: When Saul escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem after his conversion, the disciples in Jerusalem
options: were full of sympathy for him
questions.explanation: The disciples were afraid of Saul and did not believe he was a disciple.

questions.text: Paul and Barnabas were referred to as 'gods' in Lystra because they
options: were agents of the unknown God
questions.explanation: The people thought they were gods after Paul healed a crippled man.

questions.text: '...Abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity...' To which issue was the above a response?
questions.explanation: This was the response to the issue of idolatry and food.

questions.text: '... I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; with respect to the hope and resurrection of the dead I am on trial.' This was part of the address of Paul to
questions.explanation: Paul said this before the Sanhedrin.

questions.text: According to Paul, which of the following is the greatest?
questions.explanation: Paul teaches that love is the greatest of these.

questions.text: According to the creation account of Genesis 1, God charged man to
options: have dominion over all the earth
questions.explanation: God gave man dominion over all creatures and the earth.

questions.text: 'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for God made man in his own image.' This statement explains the
questions.explanation: This teaches the prohibition of murder and blood revenge.

questions.text: When God told Abraham that Sarah would have a child, Abraham laughed because
options: they were too old to have a child
he already had a child called Ishmael
questions.explanation: Abraham laughed because he and Sarah were too old to have children.

questions.text: After Jacob's dream at Bethel, he promised that he would
options: give a tenth of all he would have to God
return immediately and settle there with his family
go to his father's house in peace
questions.explanation: Jacob vowed to give a tenth of all he had to God.

questions.text: Why did Judah advise his brothers against shedding the blood of Joseph?
options: He wanted to raise some money by selling Joseph
questions.explanation: Judah suggested selling Joseph to the Ishmaelites to make money.

questions.text: Why did God redeem the Israelites from the hands of Pharaoh?
options: God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
The yoke of the Israelites was heavy
God wanted to show His power to Pharaoh
He wanted to show that Moses was powerful
questions.explanation: God remembered His covenant with the patriarchs.

questions.text: When the people of Israel saw the great work of the LORD in drowning the Egyptians, they
options: built an altar to the LORD
questions.explanation: The people believed in Moses after seeing God's power.

questions.text: The golden calf which Aaron made for the people of Israel signified
options: a return to the gods of Egypt
the final break with the god that brought them out of Egypt
the beginning of idolatry in Israel
the end of Moses' leadership of the people of Israel
questions.explanation: The golden calf represented a return to the gods of Egypt.

questions.text: During the giving of the law at Mount Sinai, the Israelites wanted Moses to speak to them instead of God because
options: the people were afraid and trembled
questions.explanation: The people were afraid they would die if God spoke directly to them.

questions.text: Where did Joshua gather all the tribes of Israel for presentation before God?
questions.explanation: Joshua gathered Israel at Shechem.

questions.text: The valley of Eshcol is symbolic to Israel because it was the place where
options: Moses and his people had a resounding victory over the Amalekites
the men of Israel cut down the cluster of grapes
the spies set out to survey Canaan
the Israelites challenged the leadership of Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: The spies cut down a cluster of grapes from the valley of Eshcol.

questions.text: The report brought by the men who followed Caleb to spy the land of Canaan showed that the land
questions.explanation: The spies reported that the land flowed with milk and honey.

questions.text: The Shema emphasizes the
options: importance of Israel to the world
questions.explanation: The Shema emphasizes the unity of God ('Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one').

questions.text: 'The LORD give you children by this woman for the loan which she lent to the LORD;...' This was said of
questions.explanation: Eli blessed Hannah that she would have more children because of Samuel.

questions.text: A good example of parental upbringing is manifested in the son of
questions.explanation: David was a good example of parental upbringing.

questions.text: The leadership potential of David was demonstrated publicly for the first time when he
options: spared King Saul's life in the cave
questions.explanation: David's leadership became known when he killed Goliath.

questions.text: Although David refused to kill Saul because he was the LORD'S anointed, he still believed that
options: Saul would be killed by the Philistines
the LORD would eventually smite Saul
Saul's soldiers would cause him to die in battle
questions.explanation: David believed the Lord would eventually deal with Saul.

questions.text: 'Blessed be you, my son David! You will do many things and will succeed in them.' The above statement was made when David
questions.explanation: Saul blessed David after David spared his life in the cave.

questions.text: Solomon asked God for wisdom to enable him
questions.explanation: Solomon asked for wisdom to discern right from wrong.

questions.text: The consequence of Rehoboam's unwise decision at the time the Israelites came to him at Shechem eventually resulted in
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's decision led to the rebellion of the northern tribes.

questions.text: The new covenant which God was to make with the house of Israel was that it would be
options: for the tribe of Judah alone
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied the new covenant written on hearts.

questions.text: According to Luke, John the Baptist instructed the multitudes that came to be baptized to
options: give thanks for being Abraham's children
questions.explanation: John told them to bear fruits worthy of repentance.

questions.text: 'Go and search diligently for the child, and when you have found him bring me word...' The intention of the speaker in this context was to
options: pay homage to the Lord Jesus
kill all the children in the area
questions.explanation: Herod intended to kill the child Jesus.

questions.text: Jesus was tempted in the wilderness in order to
options: prove that He was the Son of God
prepare Him for His earthly ministry
questions.explanation: Jesus was tempted to prepare Him for His earthly ministry.

questions.text: One important fact about Mary brought out in Jesus' miracle of changing water to wine was that she
options: must intercede for a miracle to occur
was a sister of the bridegroom
had a deep insight of her son and His ability
questions.explanation: Mary understood Jesus' power and told the servants to do whatever He said.

questions.text: The raising of Lazarus illustrates that Jesus
options: was a good friend of Lazarus
questions.explanation: Jesus demonstrated that He is the resurrection and the life.

questions.text: 'Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, ...' The continuation of this message by the centurion indicated that
options: he had faith in the power of Jesus' word
as a Gentile, he did not like the Jews
as an army officer, he wanted to avoid contact with Jesus
questions.explanation: The centurion demonstrated great faith in Jesus' word.

questions.text: The epileptic boy could not be healed by the disciples because
options: they had not yet received power
their prayers were not intensive enough
they had to wait for Jesus
questions.explanation: The disciples needed faith and prayer to cast out the demon.

questions.text: The poor in spirit are promised
questions.explanation: Jesus said the poor in spirit possess the kingdom of heaven.

questions.text: Those that are hated and reviled shall
options: have a great reward in heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus said those who suffer for His sake will have a great reward in heaven.

questions.text: Jesus' objective for sending out the twelve was
options: for them to teach the Gentiles about the God of the Jews
to train the disciples in His ministry
to demonstrate that He was about to be crucified
to divert the attention of Herod from Himself
questions.explanation: Jesus sent the twelve to train them in His ministry.

questions.text: Who appeared and talked with Jesus during the transfiguration?
questions.explanation: Moses and Elijah appeared at the transfiguration.

questions.text: 'Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory...' Why was this request by the sons of Zebedee not granted?
options: They were not qualified for the privilege
The other disciples disagreed with them
They were unable to drink the cup
It was not the duty of Jesus to grant their request
questions.explanation: Jesus said it was not His to give, but the Father's.

questions.text: At the trials of Jesus, Pilate was perplexed because
options: the Jews had no genuine case against Him
Jesus gave no answer to the charges
the Jews asked for the release of Barabbas, a notorious criminal
he knew that Jesus had performed many miracles among the Jews
questions.explanation: Pilate found no fault in Jesus but was pressured by the crowd.

questions.text: Why did the accusers of Jesus stay behind while He was led to the Praetorium?
options: It was forbidden to follow the accused
They did not want to be defiled
questions.explanation: They did not want to be defiled before the Passover.

questions.text: Who was forced to carry the cross behind Jesus?
questions.explanation: Simon of Cyrene was compelled to carry Jesus' cross.

questions.text: 'Truly I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise.' This was said to
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to the repentant robber on the cross.

questions.text: According to Luke, the people who first got to Jesus' tomb were
options: Mary the mother of Jesus, Peter and John
Mary Magdalene and the other women
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene and the other women went to the tomb first.

questions.text: Jesus Christ, the Good Shepherd was loved by the Father because He
options: understood the needs of the sheep
laid down His life for the sheep
questions.explanation: Jesus said He lays down His life for the sheep, and this is why the Father loves Him.

questions.text: Jesus said to her, 'I am the resurrection and the life: he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die...' On what occasion was this statement made?
options: On the day of Jesus' resurrection
When Jesus demonstrated the fact of His resurrection to Thomas
On the day Jesus restored Lazarus back to life
When Jairus' daughter was raised from the dead
questions.explanation: Jesus said this before raising Lazarus from the dead.

questions.text: Who said this, 'there shall be neither dew nor rain these years except by my word?'
questions.explanation: Elijah declared this to King Ahab as a judgment from God, stating that no rain or dew would come except by his word.

questions.text: In the case before Solomon over the dead and the living child, the mother of the dead child supported
options: giving the living child to her opponent.
joint ownership of the loving child.
king Solomon having the living child.
questions.explanation: The mother of the dead child, out of jealousy, agreed to give the living child to her opponent rather than see it killed.

questions.text: Before Moses died, God appointed ... to succeed him.
questions.explanation: God appointed Joshua, the son of Nun, to succeed Moses and lead the Israelites into the Promised Land.

questions.text: The treatment for those bitten by the fiery serpent was to
questions.explanation: God instructed Moses to make a bronze serpent and put it on a pole; anyone who looked at it would live.

questions.text: In order that Benjamin might be brought to Egypt, Joseph detained
questions.explanation: Joseph detained Simeon and bound him before their brothers' eyes as a guarantee that they would return with Benjamin.

questions.text: When Joseph's brother came to him in Egypt, he said to them, 'You are...'
questions.explanation: Joseph accused his brothers of being spies who came to see the weakness of the land.

questions.text: Sarah gave birth to...in her old age.
questions.explanation: Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age, fulfilling God's promise to Abraham.

questions.text: As a condition of his covenant with God, Abraham had to
questions.explanation: God commanded Abraham to circumcise every male in his household as a sign of the covenant between them.

questions.text: What was the condition of the earth before the creation of the world?
options: The earth was without form and void.
There was a firmament above the earth.
The heaven was very close to the earth.
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:2 states that the earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep.

questions.text: God wanted to destroy the world because
options: the sons of God were taking the daughters of men as wives.
the earth was filled with violence.
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:11-13 says the earth was corrupt and filled with violence, so God decided to destroy it.

questions.text: What did Adonijah do to show that he feared Solomon?
options: caught hold of the horns of the altar.
questions.explanation: When Adonijah heard that Solomon had been made king, he went and caught hold of the horns of the altar for protection.

questions.text: Where did Solomon get the timber for his building?
questions.explanation: Solomon obtained timber from Lebanon through a treaty with Hiram, king of Tyre.

questions.text: According to Jeremiah's prophecy, the domination of nations by Nebuchadnezzar was
options: the result of his military might.
the result of the wickedness of nations.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah taught that Nebuchadnezzar was God's servant and his domination was part of God's divine purpose.

topic_questions.text: The opening account of creation presents God's sovereignty most clearly through His ability to
options: delegate the entire work of creation to angels
create only things that already existed in another form
depend on human beings to complete creation
bring the universe into order by His command
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 1 portrays God creating and ordering the universe through His sovereign command.

topic_questions.text: In Genesis 1, the repeated declaration that creation was good primarily emphasizes that
options: creation reflected God's purposeful and orderly work
human beings had no special responsibility within creation
the material world existed independently of God
topic_questions.explanation: The repeated assessment of creation as good shows its purposeful order and conformity to God's will.

topic_questions.text: The creation of humanity in the image of God implies that human beings were uniquely equipped to
options: determine moral truth without divine guidance
possess the same power as the Creator
topic_questions.explanation: Being made in God's image gives humanity a distinctive role of responsible stewardship under God's authority.

topic_questions.text: Which feature of Genesis 1 most strongly distinguishes God's creative activity from ordinary human production?
options: It involved the use of previously manufactured tools
It required the assistance of other creators
It occurred through God's authoritative word
It was completed gradually by human beings
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 1 repeatedly presents God bringing aspects of creation into existence through His command.

topic_questions.text: If a society treats natural resources as possessions to exploit without responsibility, the creation account would most directly challenge that attitude by teaching
options: that humans must abandon all material resources
that only rulers may use creation
that dominion carries a responsibility of stewardship
topic_questions.explanation: Human dominion in Genesis is a responsibility to manage creation, not a licence for reckless exploitation.

topic_questions.text: The distinction between the Creator and His creation in Genesis 1 teaches that
options: creation itself is worthy of worship
God remains sovereign over everything He created
human beings are independent of God
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis distinguishes God as Creator from everything else, establishing His supreme authority over creation.

topic_questions.text: The ordering of creation in Genesis 1 is significant because it shows that
options: God's creative activity followed a purposeful sequence
humans existed before their environment was prepared
the different parts of creation were unrelated
topic_questions.explanation: The sequence presents creation as deliberate and ordered rather than accidental.

topic_questions.text: Genesis 2 contributes to the understanding of God's sovereignty by showing that
options: God remained directly involved with humanity
creation was completed without divine purpose
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 2 portrays God's continuing involvement in forming, placing and commanding humanity.

topic_questions.text: The creation of woman from man in Genesis 2 is most appropriately understood as emphasizing
options: the superiority of one sex over the other
the isolation of humanity from God
the incompatibility of man and woman
the complementary relationship intended for human companionship
topic_questions.explanation: The account emphasizes the need for suitable companionship and the complementary relationship between man and woman.

topic_questions.text: A student argues that because humans have dominion over creation, they may use nature without limits. Genesis 1 most strongly contradicts this argument because dominion
options: places humans under God's authority as stewards
means that creation has no value
topic_questions.explanation: Human dominion is exercised under God's sovereignty and therefore carries responsibility.

topic_questions.text: The phrase 'Let there be light' in the creation narrative primarily illustrates God's
topic_questions.explanation: The command demonstrates God's authority to bring creation into existence by His word.

topic_questions.text: The separation of light from darkness in Genesis 1 illustrates God's work of
options: establishing order and distinction within creation
topic_questions.explanation: The separation demonstrates God's ordering of creation into distinct and purposeful elements.

topic_questions.text: Why is God's resting on the seventh day significant within the creation account?
options: It suggests that God was defeated by creation
It proves that creation remained unfinished
It shows that humans had become sovereign
It marks the completion and goodness of His creative work
topic_questions.explanation: The seventh day follows the completion of creation and signifies its finished and ordered state.

topic_questions.text: The creation narrative would best support which view of human responsibility?
options: Humans should exercise authority without accountability
Humans should care for creation while recognizing God's ownership
Humans should avoid all interaction with nature
topic_questions.explanation: Humans are entrusted with dominion while remaining subject to God's sovereignty.

topic_questions.text: Psalm 19's description of the heavens declaring God's glory supports the creation account by emphasizing that
options: nature points to the greatness of its Creator
the heavens possess authority over God
human beings created the natural order
topic_questions.explanation: Psalm 19 presents the created order as evidence of God's glory and creative power.

topic_questions.text: A person who claims that the universe operates independently of God would be challenged by the biblical concept of sovereignty because it teaches that God
options: controls and sustains the created order
gave His authority permanently to humanity
topic_questions.explanation: Biblical sovereignty presents God as the Creator and supreme Controller of the universe.

topic_questions.text: The command for humanity to 'fill the earth and subdue it' should be understood primarily as
options: a mandate for responsible rule over creation
a command to worship the earth
topic_questions.explanation: The mandate gives humanity authority to govern creation responsibly under God.

topic_questions.text: Which conclusion follows most directly from the fact that God evaluated His completed creation as 'very good'?
options: Human beings may ignore its preservation
God's work was purposeful and harmonious
Only spiritual realities matter to God
topic_questions.explanation: The statement 'very good' indicates the purposeful harmony and quality of God's completed creation.

topic_questions.text: The creation of human beings after the preparation of the earth suggests that
options: God prepared an environment suitable for human life
humans were unnecessary to God's purpose
topic_questions.explanation: The narrative presents the environment as prepared before humanity was placed within it.

topic_questions.text: The creation account most directly undermines the claim that human beings are ultimate owners of the earth because
options: humans were created before the earth
God is presented as the original Creator and authority
the earth is presented as independent of God
humans were commanded to worship nature
topic_questions.explanation: Since God is the Creator, human authority over creation is delegated rather than absolute.

topic_questions.text: The use of different commands during creation demonstrates that God's sovereignty is expressed through
topic_questions.explanation: The commands in Genesis 1 portray God acting deliberately and authoritatively.

topic_questions.text: Genesis 2 differs in emphasis from Genesis 1 mainly because it gives greater attention to
options: the formation and relationship of human beings
the creation of stars and planets
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 2 focuses more closely on humanity, the garden, relationships and God's commands.

topic_questions.text: If creation belongs ultimately to God, which attitude toward environmental responsibility is most consistent with the biblical teaching?
options: Responsible use because humans are entrusted with God's creation
Exploitation because humans possess absolute ownership
Indifference because only spiritual matters matter
topic_questions.explanation: God's ownership and human stewardship provide a basis for responsible care of creation.

topic_questions.text: The creation account presents human dignity as closely connected with
options: being made in the image of God
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 1 connects humanity's distinctive status with being created in God's image.

topic_questions.text: Which statement best captures the biblical relationship between divine sovereignty and human responsibility?
options: Human responsibility makes God's sovereignty unnecessary
Humans are responsible to exercise delegated authority under God
Human beings and God possess identical authority
topic_questions.explanation: Biblical teaching combines God's supreme authority with humanity's responsibility to manage creation.

topic_questions.text: The ordering of creation before the appearance of humanity suggests that human life
options: has no relationship to the natural world
exists within an environment intentionally provided by God
created the conditions necessary for its existence
is superior to God's creative purpose
topic_questions.explanation: The narrative depicts God preparing the world before placing humans within it.

topic_questions.text: Isaiah's teaching that God alone is God reinforces the creation account by stressing that
options: God shares ultimate sovereignty with nature
God's sovereignty is unique and unrivalled
topic_questions.explanation: Isaiah emphasizes God's unique identity and unmatched authority over creation.

topic_questions.text: A leader who treats public resources as personal property would be acting contrary to the creation principle of stewardship because stewardship implies
options: accountable management of what belongs ultimately to God
topic_questions.explanation: Stewardship means managing entrusted resources responsibly rather than treating them as one's absolute possession.

topic_questions.text: The biblical description of creation as ordered rather than chaotic supports the conclusion that
options: creation reflects divine wisdom and intention
human beings created the universe's order
topic_questions.explanation: The orderly sequence of creation reflects God's wisdom and purposeful intention.

topic_questions.text: The creation of living creatures according to their kinds most directly indicates that
options: God exercised deliberate authority over the variety of life
all living things originated through human planning
animals possessed authority over their Creator
topic_questions.explanation: The phrase indicates deliberate differentiation within God's creative work.

topic_questions.text: A Christian who claims that faith requires contempt for the physical world would find the creation account difficult to defend because
options: God repeatedly declared aspects of creation good
Genesis teaches that matter is evil
humans were forbidden from using creation
the physical world is described as meaningless
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis repeatedly describes creation as good, rejecting the idea that the physical world is inherently worthless.

topic_questions.text: The special command given to humanity concerning the tree in Eden demonstrates that human freedom in creation
options: was exercised within God's revealed boundaries
topic_questions.explanation: The command concerning the tree shows that human freedom existed within limits established by God.

topic_questions.text: The naming of the animals by Adam in Genesis 2 is most closely associated with
options: human beings gaining independence from God
human participation in exercising delegated authority
topic_questions.explanation: Adam's naming of the animals reflects the authority and responsibility entrusted to humanity.

topic_questions.text: Which situation best illustrates the biblical concept of stewardship?
options: A farmer destroys his soil because he considers it entirely his own
A ruler uses natural resources while accepting responsibility for their preservation
A community refuses to use any natural resources
A person worships the natural environment
topic_questions.explanation: Stewardship involves responsible use and preservation rather than destruction or worship of creation.

topic_questions.text: The biblical assertion that God created both light and darkness challenges the idea that
options: God has authority over the natural order
topic_questions.explanation: The creation narrative places the natural order under God's sovereign authority.

topic_questions.text: When Genesis 1 distinguishes between the Creator and created things, it provides a basis for rejecting
topic_questions.explanation: Since created things owe their existence to God, they are not to replace the Creator as objects of worship.

topic_questions.text: The expression 'image of God' is best understood as indicating that humans
options: uniquely represent God's purposes within creation
topic_questions.explanation: Being made in God's image gives humanity a distinctive representative and responsible role in creation.

topic_questions.text: The account of creation gives the strongest basis for Christian opposition to environmental abuse because
options: nature has no connection with human life
humans are accountable for how they exercise dominion
God commanded humans to destroy creation
only animals are responsible for the environment
topic_questions.explanation: Human dominion is accountable stewardship, making destructive abuse inconsistent with the biblical mandate.

topic_questions.text: If God's sovereignty means His supreme authority over creation, which action best reflects recognition of that sovereignty?
options: Submitting human decisions to God's moral will
Treating human opinion as the highest authority
topic_questions.explanation: Recognizing God's sovereignty means acknowledging His authority and submitting human conduct to His will.

topic_questions.text: The creation of humanity as male and female within the biblical account primarily establishes that
options: human relationships form part of God's creative purpose
only one sex bears God's image
sexual distinction has no place in creation
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis presents humanity as male and female and connects human relationships with God's creative purpose.

topic_questions.text: A government introduces policies to protect forests and water resources for future generations. From a creation perspective, this is most consistent with
topic_questions.explanation: Protecting resources responsibly can reflect the stewardship entrusted to humanity.

topic_questions.text: The fact that God rested after creation should not be interpreted as weakness because the passage presents the rest as
options: a deliberate conclusion to completed work
topic_questions.explanation: The seventh-day rest follows the completion of creation and signifies completion rather than weakness.

topic_questions.text: A major implication of God's sovereignty in the creation narrative is that human beings should
options: consider themselves absolute owners of the universe
exercise authority with humility and accountability
topic_questions.explanation: Since God is the sovereign Creator, human authority must be exercised humbly and responsibly.

topic_questions.text: The statement that God formed man from the dust and gave him life most clearly communicates that human existence
topic_questions.explanation: Genesis 2 portrays human life as dependent on God's creative action and gift of life.

topic_questions.text: Which conclusion best combines the lessons of Genesis 1 and 2 concerning humanity?
options: Humans are divine rulers without limits
Humans have no special role in creation
Humans are merely passive observers of creation
Humans possess dignity and authority while remaining accountable to God
topic_questions.explanation: Both chapters present humanity as uniquely significant, entrusted with responsibility yet subject to God's authority.

topic_questions.text: The creation account would most strongly support the principle that technological advancement should
options: serve human needs while respecting responsible stewardship
give humans unlimited control over nature
topic_questions.explanation: Human creativity and authority should operate within the responsibility of caring for God's creation.

topic_questions.text: When Psalm 19 presents the heavens as declaring God's glory, it suggests that creation can function as
options: an object that possesses divine authority
topic_questions.explanation: The heavens testify to God's glory rather than replacing Him as an object of worship.

topic_questions.text: The biblical teaching on God's sovereignty would most directly challenge a worldview in which
options: human beings are accountable to a higher authority
God is regarded as the ultimate source of existence
human autonomy is treated as the highest authority
topic_questions.explanation: Divine sovereignty contradicts the idea that human autonomy is the highest or ultimate authority.

topic_questions.text: A careful reading of Genesis 1 shows that the repeated divine commands and their fulfilment emphasize the relationship between God's word and
topic_questions.explanation: The repeated pattern of divine command and fulfilment emphasizes God's authoritative power to establish creation's order.

topic_questions.text: The most appropriate Christian response to the biblical doctrine of creation is therefore to
options: worship nature because it reveals God
recognize God as Creator and live responsibly within His creation
topic_questions.explanation: The doctrine calls for recognition of God as Creator together with responsible living within His created order.

topic_questions.text: Moses' reluctance to accept God's call at the burning bush was mainly overcome by God's assurance that
options: Aaron would lead Israel without him
God Himself would be with him
topic_questions.explanation: God assured Moses that His presence would accompany him in the mission.

topic_questions.text: Moses' request for signs before confronting Pharaoh reveals that effective leadership may require
options: recognition of personal limitations and dependence on God
